events.title: Nicolaus Copernicus is born
events.description: The astronomer was born in Toruń, in Royal Prussia. He grew up to propose that the Sun, not the Earth, sits at the center of the universe.
events.significance: His heliocentric theory launched the Scientific Revolution and changed how humanity understands its place in the cosmos.

events.title: Edison patents the phonograph
events.description: Thomas Edison was granted U.S. Patent No. 200,521 for his phonograph, a machine that could record sound and play it back.
events.significance: It was the first device to record and reproduce sound. It paved the way for the modern recorded-music industry.

events.title: Roosevelt signs Executive Order 9066
events.description: During World War II, President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the order. It authorized the military to designate exclusion zones and led to the removal and internment of about 125,000 people of Japanese ancestry, many of them U.S. citizens.
events.significance: It remains one of the most notorious civil-liberties violations in American history. It led to later formal apologies and reparations.

events.title: U.S. Marines land on Iwo Jima
events.description: Operation Detachment began as the first waves of U.S. Marines came ashore on the volcanic Pacific island. The result was a month-long battle against Japanese defenders.
events.significance: It was one of the bloodiest battles of the Pacific War. It also produced some of the war's most iconic imagery.

events.title: Harper Lee dies
events.description: The author of To Kill a Mockingbird died at age 89. She had spent most of her later life out of the public eye.
events.significance: Her Pulitzer Prize-winning novel is still a cornerstone of American literature. It continues to shape conversations about justice and racial equality.
